title: Truth-table and weak truth-table reductions

based_on.title: Lecture notes in Computability Theory
based_on.pages: Definition 34.11 and Proposition 34.12, pp. 82–83; version dated December 3, 2008

based_on.title: Random Strings and Truth-Table Degrees of Turing Complete C.E. Sets

authors: University of Wisconsin–Madison, Department of Mathematics
based_on.title: Logic Qualifying Exam, Computability

summary: Compare finite truth tables with oracle programs whose successful query positions have a computable bound, and characterize truth-table reducibility by all-oracle termination.
abstract: An oracle program may ask a second question only after seeing the answer to its first. A truth-table reduction instead fixes a finite list of possible questions and a rule for combining all their answers before the oracle is consulted. A weak truth-table reduction permits more dependence on the answers, but requires a computable bound on the positions queried in every successful computation for the supplied oracle. We compare these two restrictions, prove that each survives composition and Boolean operations, and show that truth tables are exactly the decision procedures that can be made to terminate for every oracle. The distinction concerns both information and termination: reversing one oracle bit already goes beyond many-one translation, while a computable bound on query positions alone need not make the same program halt for other oracles.
